key_insight: Real patient-chatbot interactions are highly diverse, and that diversity can materially change LLM triage outcomes.
engineering_relevance: Health chatbot systems should be designed and evaluated to model not just clinical content, but also emotion, strategy, and communication style to better match real-world use.
method: Analyzed 2,053 real patient-chatbot conversations to characterize variation in user communication patterns.
Built a patient simulator that separately models clinical content, emotional state, conversational strategy, and communication style.
Tested realism with 15 human graders and assessed urgency performance across 1,164 clinician-graded cases using five patient personae and four LLMs.
evidence_signal: In a Turing-inspired realism test, human graders identified simulated versus real conversations with only 55% accuracy, and communication style significantly altered triage outcomes.
watch_item: Evaluations based on idealized or cooperative patient personas may overestimate performance and could miss disparities caused by realistic communication diversity.
paper_title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
